howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 62.0% of the ball and 66.9% of the passing in the opposition half, against a season average of 62.7%.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Ipswich Town's 4-2-3-1 (6 changes from the Leeds game, switching from 4-3-3).
The result matched the chances: 2.65 xG to 0.47.
Compared with their other league games, Spurs created better-quality chances (0.15 vs 0.08), conceded less (0.47 xG vs 1.19 xG), went long more often (4.4% vs 3.4%).
Solanke was the biggest attacking threat (1.35 xG + xA); Fernandes won the ball back most often (7 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 62% of the ball (season average 63%), completing 525 of 590 passes (89%).
67% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), in line with their usual 70%. They spent long spells camped in Ipswich Town's half.
49% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (258 own half, 267 opposition half): most of the passing happened high up the pitch.
Long balls made up 4.4% of accurate passes (in line with the season's 3.4%), with 59% of long balls finding a teammate.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 18 shots (9 on target) worth 2.65 xG, 0.15 per shot; the season average is 0.08 per shot, so the chances were better quality than usual.
16 shots came from inside the box and 2 from outside (11% from distance).
Spurs created 3 big chances and missed 1 (season average 2.3).
36 touches in Ipswich Town's box, above the season average of 32; Ipswich Town had 21 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 2.05 (76%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.66. 8 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 2 from 2.65 xG: 0.6 fewer than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 3.99 xGOT against 2.65 xG before the shot: the finishing placed shots better than average.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 4.0 Ipswich Town passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.1. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was Spurs' usual pressing level.
18 tackles won and 5 interceptions (season averages 17.5 and 7.5); 17 clearances and 8 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 54, Ipswich Town 54 (50% for Spurs); 57% of aerial duels won.
Ipswich Town managed 11 shots worth 0.47 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.19 xG) and 0 big chances.

phases.title: Transitions and set pieces

Set pieces: 8 Spurs shots (0.66 xG, 0 goals); Ipswich Town 3 (0.09 xG, 0 goals). Corners: 8–6.

flow: First half: 1.52 xG for, 0.13 against (1–0). Second half: 1.19 for, 0.25 against (1–0).
Spells on top (momentum index): Spurs 7–32'; Spurs 49–57'; Spurs 70–78'.
